mainTopic: A מגילה written inside a scroll of כתובים, the limit of 'בציבור שנו', the הלכה למשה מסיני about leaving the edges of a ספר תורה unstitched, and an אגדה about the cave of משה and אליהו
overview: This amud opens at the end of a story. לוי בר שמואל read the מגילה from a scroll that held all the כתובים, and רב יהודה told him it does not count. Then רבי חייא בר אבא reports several teachings in the name of רבי יוחנן. First, a combined scroll does not count, but 'ומחו לה אמוחא' limits this to a public reading. Second, leaving the edges of a ספר תורה unsewn is a הלכה למשה מסיני, but it exists only to keep the parchment from tearing. Third, an אגדה: even a pinhole in the cave of משה and אליהו would have let in too much light. Fourth, משה was shown at סיני even the future laws of the סופרים, such as מקרא מגילה. Next comes a new משנה: everyone may read the מגילה except a חרש, a שוטה and a קטן, and רבי יהודה allows a קטן. The גמרא asks whose view excludes a חרש even בדיעבד. It goes back and forth between רבי יוסי and רבי יהודה, and ends with two ברייתות, about תרומה and about ברכת המזון, that no single reading of רבי יהודה can fit. The resolution comes on the next amud.

steps.title: רב יהודה rules that a מגילה written among the כתובים does not count
steps.stepSummary: The story from the previous daf ends here. לוי בר שמואל read from a מגילה written inside a scroll of all the כתובים, and רב יהודה tells him he has not fulfilled his obligation.
steps.simpleTranslation: [He was reading from a מגילה] written among the כתובים. רב יהודה said to him: The חכמים have said that one who reads from a מגילה written among the כתובים has not fulfilled his obligation.
steps.whatsHappening: The first words finish a sentence that began on the previous daf: לוי בר שמואל was reading before רב יהודה from a combined scroll. רב יהודה then corrects him with a known ruling.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The problem is not the text itself, because every word of אסתר was there. The problem is that the מגילה was not its own separate scroll; it was one book inside a larger scroll of כתובים. רב יהודה quotes an existing teaching ('הרי אמרו') that such a reading does not fulfill the obligation.

keyTerms.meaning: written among the Writings, meaning in one scroll together with the other books of כתובים
'Behold, they have said', used to quote an established ruling of the Sages
he did not fulfill his obligation
scroll; here, מגילת אסתר

steps.confusionAlert: This amud starts in the middle of a sentence. The words 'הכתובה בין הכתובים' finish a story from the previous daf, where לוי בר שמואל was reading in front of רב יהודה. 'He said to him' means רב יהודה said to לוי.

phrases.english: [from a Megillah] that was written among the Writings.
phrases.notes: This finishes a sentence from the previous daf, where לוי בר שמואל was reading before רב יהודה.

phrases.english: He (Rav Yehuda) said to him: Behold, they have said,
One who reads from a Megillah
that is written among the Writings
has not fulfilled his obligation.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Finishes a story that began on the previous daf.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Reading from a מגילה that is part of a combined scroll of כתובים does not fulfill the obligation.

steps.title: רבי יוחנן states the same rule
steps.stepSummary: רבי חייא בר אבא reports in the name of רבי יוחנן the same ruling: reading from a מגילה written among the כתובים does not fulfill the obligation.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי חייא בר אבא said in the name of רבי יוחנן: One who reads from a מגילה written among the כתובים has not fulfilled his obligation.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings an אמורא from ארץ ישראל who holds the same rule that רב יהודה used. This statement also sets up the limit that comes in the next line.
steps.deeperAnalysis: So far the rule sounds complete, with no exceptions. The next line will right away narrow it.

keyTerms.meaning: an אמורא who often passes on teachings of רבי יוחנן
the leading אמורא of ארץ ישראל

phrases.english: Rabbi Chiyya bar Abba said
that Rabbi Yochanan said:
One who reads from a Megillah
that is written among the Writings
has not fulfilled his obligation.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַבִּי חִיָּיא בַּר אַבָּא אָמַר רַבִּי יוֹחָנָן
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Supports רב יהודה's ruling with the same rule from רבי יוחנן.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: A מגילה written among the כתובים is not valid for the reading.

steps.title: The rule is limited to public reading
steps.stepSummary: Right away, a limit is added: the rule was taught only for reading before a צבור. A person reading alone does fulfill his obligation with such a scroll.
steps.simpleTranslation: But they hit it on its head: they taught this only for a congregation.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא narrows the rule it just stated. It applies only to a public reading.
steps.deeperAnalysis: 'ומחו לה אמוחא' means a limit was attached to the rule as soon as it was said, taking away much of its force. For a צבור, the reading must be from a מגילה that is its own scroll. A single person reading privately is still יוצא with a combined scroll.

keyTerms.meaning: 'and they struck it on its brain', meaning they right away qualified the rule and weakened it
they taught it only about a congregation
congregation; a public reading

steps.confusionAlert: 'ומחו לה אמוחא' does not cancel the rule. The rule still stands, but only in a narrower case: a public reading.
steps.whyThisMatters: The practical הלכה depends on this: an individual may read from a combined scroll, but a public reading needs a separate מגילה.

phrases.english: And they struck it on its head:
They taught it only regarding a congregation.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Limits the rule from step 2.
steps.dechiyaRejectionScope: Partial. It keeps the rule but limits it to a public reading.
steps.dechiyaFlawIdentified: The plain rule seemed to apply to everyone, but in fact it applies only before a צבור.
steps.maskanaFinalTakeaway: Only a public reading requires a separate מגילה.

steps.title: Leaving the edges unstitched is a law from Sinai
steps.stepSummary: רבי יוחנן teaches that leaving the top and bottom edges of the sheets of a ספר תורה unsewn is a הלכה למשה מסיני.
steps.simpleTranslation: And רבי חייא בר אבא said in the name of רבי יוחנן: Leaving a part without stitching is a law given to משה at סיני.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a second teaching from the same chain of transmission, this time about how the sheets of a ספר תורה are sewn together.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The sheets of parchment are sewn to each other, but a small gap must be left at the top and bottom. Calling this a הלכה למשה מסיני makes it sound like a deep law of the scroll's holiness. The next line will limit that.

keyTerms.meaning: leaving a section without stitches at the edges of the sheets
a law received orally by משה at Sinai, not written in the תורה
stitching; seam

phrases.english: And Rabbi Chiyya bar Abba said
that Rabbi Yochanan said:
Leaving over [unstitched space] in the seam
is a law given to Moshe at Sinai.

steps.triggerLanguage: וְאָמַר רַבִּי חִיָּיא בַּר אַבָּא אָמַר רַבִּי יוֹחָנָן
steps.relationToPreviousStep: A new teaching, grouped here because it comes through the same chain of transmission and follows the same 'ומחו לה אמוחא' pattern.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Leaving the edges unstitched is a הלכה למשה מסיני.

steps.title: The unstitched edges are only to prevent tearing
steps.stepSummary: Right away, a limit is added: the purpose of the rule is practical, to keep the parchment from tearing.
steps.simpleTranslation: But they hit it on its head: they said this only so that it should not tear.
steps.whatsHappening: The same 'hit on its head' pattern appears again, now limiting the purpose of the הלכה למשה מסיני.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The rule is not about the special holiness of the scroll. If the seams ran all the way to the edge, rolling the scroll too tightly would rip the parchment. The unsewn gap gives a warning by spreading apart first, so the person rolling it eases off.

keyTerms.meaning: they said it only for this purpose
so that it should not tear

steps.whatToRemember: There is a pattern here: רבי יוחנן states a strong rule, and 'ומחו לה אמוחא' right away narrows it, either in who it applies to (only a צבור) or in its purpose (only to prevent tearing).

phrases.english: And they struck it on its head:
They only said it
so that it should not tear.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Limits the purpose of the rule from step 4.
steps.dechiyaRejectionScope: Partial. The rule still stands, but its reason is practical.
steps.dechiyaFlawIdentified: One might think the rule comes from the holiness of the scroll, but its real purpose is to protect the parchment.
steps.maskanaFinalTakeaway: The unsewn edges exist to keep the ספר תורה from tearing.

steps.title: The cave of משה and אליהו
steps.stepSummary: An אגדה from רבי יוחנן: if even a tiny crack had been open in the cave where משה and אליהו stood, they could not have survived the light of the שכינה.
steps.simpleTranslation: And רבי חייא בר אבא said in the name of רבי יוחנן: Had even a crack the size of a fine needle's hole been left in the cave where משה and אליהו stood, they could not have endured the light, as it says: 'For no man shall see Me and live.'
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא adds a third teaching from the same chain of transmission. This one is not הלכה but an אגדה about the revelation to משה and אליהו.
steps.deeperAnalysis: משה and אליהו both stood in a cave or cleft of rock when the שכינה passed by. רבי יוחנן says the closed rock protected them completely, because even a pinhole of that light would have overwhelmed them. He proves this from the פסוק 'כי לא יראני האדם וחי'.

keyTerms.meaning: had it been that; if only
cave
the hole of a fine sewing needle
light; here, the radiance of the שכינה
as it is said; introduces a פסוק

phrases.english: And Rabbi Chiyya bar Abba said
that Rabbi Yochanan said:
Had there been left open in the cave
in which Moshe and Eliyahu stood
even the size of the hole of a fine sewing needle,
they would not have been able to endure
because of the light,
as it is said: 'For no man shall see Me
and live.'

steps.triggerLanguage: וְאָמַר רַבִּי חִיָּיא בַּר אַבָּא אָמַר רַבִּי יוֹחָנָן
steps.relationToPreviousStep: A third teaching from the same chain of transmission, brought here because it is grouped with the others.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The cave protected משה and אליהו completely; even a pinhole of the שכינה's light would have been more than they could bear.

steps.title: ה׳ showed משה even the future rabbinic laws, like reading the מגילה
steps.stepSummary: רבי חייא בר אבא, quoting רבי יוחנן, explains a פסוק to mean that משה was shown the fine points of the תורה, the fine points of the סופרים, and the new laws the סופרים would add in the future. The example of such a future law is מקרא מגילה.
steps.simpleTranslation: And רבי חייא בר אבא said in the name of רבי יוחנן: What does the פסוק mean, "and on them, according to all the words which ה׳ spoke with you on the mountain"? It teaches that הקדוש ברוך הוא showed משה the fine details of the תורה, the fine details of the סופרים, and what the סופרים would one day introduce. And what is that? The reading of the מגילה.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings one more teaching of רבי יוחנן, the last in this series. It reads a פסוק as saying that משה was shown even the laws the rabbis would add later, such as reading the מגילה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The extra words "כְּכׇל הַדְּבָרִים" ("according to ALL the words") are read as including more than the written תורה. They include rabbinic details and future rabbinic laws too. The short question "וּמַאי נִיהוּ?" asks for an example, and the answer is מקרא מגילה, which ties the דרשה back to our מסכתא.

keyTerms.meaning: The fine details and inferences that come from the words of the תורה
The fine details and inferences of the early rabbis (the סופרים)
Will introduce in the future (new rabbinic laws)
The reading of מגילת אסתר
This teaches (introduces what a פסוק comes to teach)

steps.confusionAlert: This does not mean that מקרא מגילה is a law from the תורה. It is still a rabbinic law. The point is only that משה was already shown, at סיני, that the rabbis would one day make it.
steps.whyThisMatters: It gives rabbinic laws like מקרא מגילה a deep root: they were foreseen and shown to משה at סיני.

phrases.english: And Rabbi Chiya bar Abba said
Rabbi Yochanan said:
What is the meaning of what is written:
phrases.notes: The verse being quoted is in דברים ט:י.

phrases.english: "And on them, according to all the words
which ה׳ spoke with you on the mountain"

phrases.aramaic: מְלַמֵּד שֶׁהֶרְאָהוּ הַקָּדוֹשׁ בָּרוּךְ הוּא לְמֹשֶׁה
phrases.english: This teaches that the Holy One, Blessed be He, showed Moshe
the fine details of the Torah
and the fine details of the Scribes
and what the Scribes would introduce in the future.
And what is that?
The reading of the Megillah.

steps.triggerLanguage: וְאָמַר רַבִּי חִיָּיא בַּר אַבָּא אָמַר רַבִּי יוֹחָנָן: מַאי דִּכְתִיב
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Continues the series of רבי יוחנן teachings (Steps 2–6). This one is a דרשה that ties back to מקרא מגילה.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: משה was shown at סיני the details of the תורה, the details of the סופרים, and future rabbinic laws such as מקרא מגילה.

steps.title: New משנה: who is fit to read the מגילה
steps.stepSummary: The משנה rules that everyone may read the מגילה except a חרש, a שוטה, and a קטן. רבי יהודה allows a קטן.
steps.simpleTranslation: משנה: Everyone is fit to read the מגילה, except a deaf person, a mentally incompetent person, and a minor. רבי יהודה allows a minor.
steps.whatsHappening: A new משנה starts. It tells us who is allowed to read the מגילה for others.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The general rule is that everyone is fit. Three exceptions are listed: חרש, שוטה, and קטן. רבי יהודה disagrees only about the קטן and says a minor may read. The משנה does not say whether the exclusion of the חרש applies even after the fact, and the גמרא will now ask about that.

keyTerms.meaning: Everyone is fit / valid
A deaf person (here, one who speaks but cannot hear)
A person lacking mental competence
A minor (below the age of מצוות)
Declares fit / allows

steps.confusionAlert: In this sugya the חרש is understood as someone who can speak but cannot hear himself. That is why the גמרא will compare him to someone who says שמע without hearing his own words.

phrases.aramaic: מַתְנִי׳ הַכֹּל כְּשֵׁרִין לִקְרוֹת אֶת הַמְּגִילָּה,
phrases.english: MISHNAH: Everyone is fit to read the Megillah,
except for a deaf person, an imbecile, and a minor.
Rabbi Yehudah declares a minor fit.

steps.triggerLanguage: מַתְנִי׳ הַכֹּל כְּשֵׁרִין לִקְרוֹת אֶת הַמְּגִילָּה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: A new topic opens: who may read the מגילה. It is not tied to the רבי יוחנן series.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Everyone is fit to read the מגילה except a חרש, a שוטה, and a קטן. רבי יהודה allows a קטן.

steps.title: Which תנא says a deaf person's reading fails even after the fact?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא assumes the משנה means a חרש's reading is invalid even בדיעבד, and asks which תנא holds that view.
steps.simpleTranslation: גמרא: Who is the תנא who taught that a deaf person's reading does not count, even after the fact?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא opens by asking whose opinion the משנה follows regarding the חרש. This question sets up the answer that comes next.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The גמרא reads the משנה as saying a חרש is not fit even בדיעבד. In other words, if he already read, it still does not count. Since such a strict view needs a source, the גמרא looks for the תנא who holds it.

keyTerms.meaning: Who is the תנא (whose opinion is this)?
After the fact, once it was already done
Also not / not even

phrases.english: GEMARA: Who is the Tanna that taught
that a deaf person, even after the fact, is not valid?

steps.triggerLanguage: מַאן תְּנָא חֵרֵשׁ דִּיעֲבַד נָמֵי לָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Asks about the משנה's ruling that a חרש is not fit.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Which תנא holds that a חרש's reading is invalid even בדיעבד.

steps.title: רב מתנה: it is רבי יוסי, who requires hearing your own words
steps.stepSummary: רב מתנה says the משנה follows רבי יוסי. In ברכות, רבי יוסי holds that one who says שמע without hearing his own words has not fulfilled his obligation.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב מתנה said: It is רבי יוסי. As we learned in a משנה: one who reads שמע but did not let his ears hear it has fulfilled his obligation. רבי יוסי says: he has not fulfilled it.
steps.whatsHappening: רב מתנה answers the question: the משנה follows רבי יוסי. He proves it from a משנה about קריאת שמע.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In ברכות, the first opinion (that of רבי יהודה) says that saying שמע without hearing it still counts. רבי יוסי says it does not count. A חרש can never hear himself, so according to רבי יוסי his reading fails even בדיעבד, which fits our משנה. The גמרא assumes that מקרא מגילה works like קריאת שמע on this point.

keyTerms.meaning: As we learned in a משנה
Made it heard to his own ears
He fulfilled his obligation

phrases.aramaic: אָמַר רַב מַתְנָה: רַבִּי יוֹסֵי הִיא,
phrases.english: Rav Masna said: It is Rabbi Yosei,
as we learned in a Mishnah:
phrases.notes: You can find this משנה in ברכות 15a.

phrases.english: One who recites the Shema
and did not make it audible to his ears has fulfilled his obligation,
phrases.notes: This first opinion is that of רבי יהודה

phrases.english: Rabbi Yosei says: He has not fulfilled it.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַב מַתְנָה: רַבִּי יוֹסֵי הִיא, דִּתְנַן
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question of Step 9.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: The משנה follows רבי יוסי, who holds that one who does not hear his own words has not fulfilled his obligation, even בדיעבד.

steps.title: Maybe the משנה is רבי יהודה, banning the deaf only at the outset
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא challenges רב מתנה's starting assumption. Perhaps the משנה follows רבי יהודה and means only that a חרש should not read לכתחילה, but after the fact his reading is fine.
steps.simpleTranslation: But how do you know it is רבי יוסי, and that it is invalid even after the fact? Maybe it is רבי יהודה, and it means only that a deaf person should not read in the first place, but after the fact it is fine?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא questions the basic assumption behind the last answer. It suggests another way to read the משנה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רב מתנה's answer depended on reading "חוץ מחרש" as "invalid even בדיעבד." The גמרא points out that the words could also mean only "not לכתחילה." If so, the משנה fits רבי יהודה, who says that not hearing oneself is acceptable after the fact. So the proof for רבי יוסי is no longer certain.

keyTerms.meaning: And from where (do you know)?
Perhaps
In the first place, ideally
It is fine / acceptable

steps.confusionAlert: Keep the two levels apart. לכתחילה means "should he do it in the first place?" בדיעבד means "if he already did it, does it count?" The whole challenge depends on which of these the משנה means.

phrases.english: But from where do you know that it is Rabbi Yosei
and that even after the fact it is not valid?
Perhaps it is Rabbi Yehudah,
and it is only at the outset that he may not read,
but after the fact, it is acceptable?

steps.triggerLanguage: וּמִמַּאי דְּרַבִּי יוֹסֵי הִיא וְדִיעֲבַד נָמֵי לָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Attacks the assumption behind Steps 9–10 that the משנה means "invalid even בדיעבד."
steps.kashyaTarget: The assumption that the משנה's exclusion of a חרש applies even בדיעבד, and so must follow רבי יוסי.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The משנה's wording could mean only "not לכתחילה," which fits רבי יהודה. So nothing forces us to say it follows רבי יוסי.

steps.title: A deaf person is grouped with an imbecile and a minor
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא rejects the challenge from step 11. Since the משנה lists חרש alongside שוטה and קטן, all three must have the same status: invalid even after the fact.
steps.simpleTranslation: That cannot be, because the משנה teaches a deaf person in the same list as an imbecile and a minor. Just as an imbecile and a minor are not valid even after the fact, so too a deaf person is not valid even after the fact.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא pushes back against the idea that the משנה only means a חרש should not read לכתחילה. It points to how the משנה groups the three people together.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A שוטה and a קטן are clearly invalid even בדיעבד. Since the משנה puts the חרש in the same list, he must have the same rule. That means the משנה really does follow רבי יוסי, as רב מתנה said.

keyTerms.meaning: This should not enter your mind (a firm rejection)
Similar to, like
A person who is mentally incompetent (imbecile)
After the fact

phrases.english: This should not enter your mind,
because it teaches a deaf person similar to an imbecile and a minor:
phrases.notes: They are listed together in one phrase in the משנה.

phrases.aramaic: מָה שׁוֹטֶה וְקָטָן — דִּיעֲבַד נָמֵי לָא,
phrases.english: just as an imbecile and a minor are not valid even after the fact,
so too a deaf person is not valid even after the fact.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Rejects the challenge of step 11 and restores רב מתנה's reading.
steps.dechiyaRejectionScope: Rejects the suggestion that the משנה means only לכתחילה for a חרש.
steps.dechiyaFlawIdentified: It ignores that the משנה groups חרש with שוטה and קטן, who are invalid even בדיעבד.

steps.title: Perhaps each person in the list has his own rule
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks whether the grouping proves anything. Perhaps שוטה and קטן are invalid even after the fact, while a חרש is only barred לכתחילה.
steps.simpleTranslation: But perhaps this one is as it is, and that one is as it is!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא challenges the proof from the list. Being listed together does not have to mean having the exact same rule.
steps.deeperAnalysis: All three are barred from reading at the start, which could be why they are listed together. After the fact, though, they might differ. The חרש's reading might count, which would let the משנה follow רבי יהודה.

keyTerms.meaning: But perhaps (introduces a challenge)
This one as it is, and that one as it is (each case keeps its own rule)

steps.confusionAlert: Listing items together in a משנה does not always mean they share every detail of their law. That is exactly the gap this challenge is pointing out.

phrases.english: But perhaps this one is as it is,
and that one is as it is!
phrases.notes: He means: a שוטה and a קטן don't count even after the fact, but a חרש is only kept out from the start (לכתחילה).

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Attacks the proof given in step 12.
steps.kashyaTarget: The inference that being listed together means having the same status.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: Items can be grouped for a shared לכתחילה rule while still differing בדיעבד, so the חרש's reading could be valid after the fact, as רבי יהודה holds.

steps.title: The first part of the משנה cannot be רבי יהודה
steps.stepSummary: The end of the משנה names רבי יהודה as disagreeing about a קטן. So the first part, which is unnamed, must belong to someone else.
steps.simpleTranslation: Since the last part teaches 'רבי יהודה declares a minor valid,' we can conclude that the first part is not רבי יהודה.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers the challenge by looking at how the משנה is built. A named opinion at the end shows the unnamed opinion at the start is someone else's.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The challenge needed the first part of the משנה to be רבי יהודה's view. However, the משנה itself quotes רבי יהודה at the end as a separate opinion. That signals the opening ruling is not his, so we cannot read the חרש rule according to him.

keyTerms.meaning: The latter clause of a משנה
The first clause of a משנה
Declares valid
By implication, it follows that

phrases.english: From the fact that the latter clause teaches:
Rabbi Yehuda declares a minor valid —

phrases.aramaic: מִכְּלָל דְּרֵישָׁא לָאו רַבִּי יְהוּדָה הִיא.
phrases.english: it follows that the first clause is not Rabbi Yehuda.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge of step 13.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Structural inference from the משנה's wording
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The unnamed first clause might be רבי יהודה, who accepts a חרש בדיעבד.
steps.terutzMaskana: Because רבי יהודה is quoted separately in the סיפא, the רישא is a different תנא.

steps.title: Perhaps the whole משנה is רבי יהודה
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא suggests that both parts could still be רבי יהודה. The first part would be stated without a name, and the second part with his name.
steps.simpleTranslation: But perhaps the whole משנה is רבי יהודה!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא challenges the answer of step 14. Quoting רבי יהודה at the end does not have to mean the beginning is someone else.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Sometimes a משנה states a ruling without a name and then names the תנא who said it. If so, the whole משנה could be רבי יהודה, and the חרש rule might again mean only לכתחילה.

keyTerms.meaning: All of it, the entire משנה
The first, unnamed תנא of a משנה

phrases.english: But perhaps the whole of it is Rabbi Yehuda!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Attacks the structural proof of step 14.
steps.kashyaTarget: The inference that naming רבי יהודה in the סיפא excludes him from the רישא.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: A משנה can open without a name and then attribute the same view by name, so both clauses could be his.

steps.title: The two parts contradict each other about a minor
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא answers that the two parts cannot be the same person. The first part disqualifies a קטן and the second part declares a קטן valid.
steps.simpleTranslation: Are they comparable? The first part is to disqualify, and the last part is to declare valid.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers the challenge by showing that the two parts of the משנה disagree about a קטן.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The רישא lists קטן as invalid, while the סיפא has רבי יהודה declaring a קטן valid. One person cannot hold both positions. So the רישא is not רבי יהודה.

keyTerms.meaning: Is it comparable? (rhetorical: they are not alike)
Invalid, disqualified
Valid, fit

phrases.english: Are they comparable?
The first clause is to disqualify,
and the latter clause is to declare valid.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge of step 15.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The whole משנה could be רבי יהודה, first without his name and then with it.
steps.terutzMaskana: The רישא disqualifies a קטן and the סיפא validates one, so they cannot be the same תנא.

steps.title: Perhaps the משנה speaks of two kinds of minors
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא suggests the whole משנה is רבי יהודה after all. It would be talking about two kinds of קטן and would be missing some words. A young קטן is invalid, while a קטן old enough for חינוך may read even לכתחילה.
steps.simpleTranslation: But perhaps the whole משנה is רבי יהודה, and it teaches two kinds of minors. The משנה is missing words and should be read like this: Everyone is fit to read the מגילה except a deaf person, an imbecile, and a minor. When is this said? About a minor who has not reached the age of training. But a minor who has reached the age of training may read even from the start, as רבי יהודה declares a minor valid.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא makes a new attempt to fit the whole משנה with רבי יהודה. It removes the contradiction from step 16 by saying the two parts are about different kinds of minors. The next steps (18–21) test this suggestion.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The contradiction disappears if the רישא is about a young קטן and the סיפא is about an older one. To make this work, the גמרא reads the משנה as if some words are missing (חסורי מחסרא). If this holds, רבי יהודה could be the author of the חרש rule, and a חרש's reading might be valid בדיעבד, which would undo רב מתנה's proof.

keyTerms.meaning: Two kinds, two types
The text is missing words, and this is what it teaches
In what case are these words said? (limits a ruling)
Reached the age of training in מצוות
From the start, ideally

steps.confusionAlert: The last line, 'שרבי יהודה מכשיר בקטן,' is not a separate opinion in this reading. It is the reason for the line before it, so the whole משנה becomes one voice.

phrases.english: But perhaps the whole of it is Rabbi Yehuda,
and it teaches two kinds of minor,
and it is missing words, and this is what it teaches:
Everyone is fit to read the Megillah
except a deaf person, an imbecile, and a minor,
In what case are these words said?
About a minor who has not reached the age of training,
but a minor who has reached the age of training —
may read even from the start.
For Rabbi Yehuda declares a minor valid.
phrases.notes: In this version of the text, this line explains why the line before it is true.

steps.triggerLanguage: וְדִלְמָא כּוּלַּהּ רַבִּי יְהוּדָה הִיא, וּתְרֵי גַוְונֵי קָטָן קָתָנֵי לַהּ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gets around the contradiction of step 16 by splitting קטן into two cases.
steps.kashyaTarget: The proof in step 16 that the רישא and סיפא contradict each other.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: If the רישא means a young קטן and the סיפא means a קטן who reached חינוך, there is no contradiction. Then the whole משנה could be רבי יהודה, and the חרש rule could be only לכתחילה.
steps.whyThisMatters: If this reading holds, רב מתנה's claim that the משנה follows רבי יוסי loses its support. Steps 18–21 test whether רבי יהודה can really be read this way.

steps.title: Pinning down what the last suggestion means
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא restates the suggestion from Step 17. If the משנה follows רבי יהודה, a חרש is barred only לכתחילה, and his reading still counts בדיעבד.
steps.simpleTranslation: How did you explain the משנה? As following רבי יהודה, so that a חרש is barred only at the start, and after the fact his reading counts?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא locks in exactly what the last suggestion commits us to. This is a setup line that prepares the attack in the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Step 17 said the משנה follows רבי יהודה. רבי יהודה holds that saying words without hearing them works בדיעבד. So a חרש, who cannot hear himself, would be barred only לכתחילה, and the גמרא is making that position explicit so it can test it.

keyTerms.meaning: How did you establish it? (asking which opinion a source was assigned to)
After the fact (once it was already done)
From the outset (the ideal way to act)

steps.confusionAlert: Background: רבי יהודה and רבי יוסי argue about someone who says קריאת שמע without hearing his own words. רבי יוסי says it does not count at all. רבי יהודה says it counts בדיעבד. A חרש is treated like someone who says words without hearing them.

phrases.english: In what way did you establish it?
As Rabbi Yehuda, and so valid after the fact?
phrases.notes: In other words: a deaf person is barred only from the outset.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Spells out what the Step 17 reading implies for a חרש, as preparation for a challenge.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Confirms that under the רבי יהודה reading, a חרש's reading counts בדיעבד but is not allowed לכתחילה.

steps.title: A deaf person separating תרומה from the outset fits no one
steps.stepSummary: A ברייתא says a חרש who speaks but cannot hear may separate תרומה even לכתחילה. רבי יהודה would allow only בדיעבד, and רבי יוסי would not allow even בדיעבד. So who wrote this ברייתא?
steps.simpleTranslation: But what about the ברייתא taught by רבי יהודה son of רבי שמעון בן פזי? 'A deaf person who speaks but does not hear may separate תרומה from the outset.' Whose view is that? If רבי יהודה, he allows it only after the fact, not from the outset. If רבי יוסי, he does not allow it even after the fact.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a ברייתא that seems to match neither רבי יהודה nor רבי יוסי as we now understand them.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Separating תרומה involves saying a ברכה, which the חרש cannot hear. The ברייתא allows it even לכתחילה. If רבי יהודה only allows such speech בדיעבד, then no known opinion supports this ברייתא. That suggests we may have understood רבי יהודה too narrowly.

keyTerms.meaning: A deaf person who can speak but cannot hear
Separates תרומה (the portion of produce given to a כהן)
Whose view is this?

phrases.english: But that which (Rabbi) Yehuda taught,
the son of Rabbi Shimon ben Pazi:
A deaf person who speaks but does not hear
may separate teruma from the outset. Whose view is this?
If it is Rabbi Yehuda,
after the fact yes, from the outset no.

phrases.aramaic: אִי רַבִּי יוֹסֵי — דִּיעֲבַד נָמֵי לָא.
phrases.english: If it is Rabbi Yosei, even after the fact no.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Attacks the position spelled out in Step 18, namely that רבי יהודה allows only בדיעבד.
steps.kashyaTarget: The claim that רבי יהודה allows speech without hearing only בדיעבד.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: A ברייתא allows a חרש to act even לכתחילה. Under our understanding, neither רבי יהודה nor רבי יוסי could hold that, so the ברייתא has no author.

steps.title: Should we say רבי יהודה allows it even from the outset?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא considers the way out: maybe רבי יהודה allows speech without hearing even לכתחילה.
steps.simpleTranslation: Rather, what would you say instead? That רבי יהודה allows it even from the outset?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא raises the obvious fix to the last problem. It is preparing to show that this fix creates a new problem.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If רבי יהודה permits even לכתחילה, the תרומה ברייתא would fit him well. The phrase 'ואלא מאי' signals that this fix will not work either. The next step explains why.

keyTerms.meaning: But rather, what? (a pushback that tests the alternative)

phrases.english: But rather, what? Rabbi Yehuda
allows it even from the outset?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Proposes the natural fix to the Step 19 challenge so it can be tested.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Whether the solution is to say רבי יהודה permits speech without hearing even לכתחילה.

steps.title: Silent ברכת המזון would then fit no one
steps.stepSummary: A ברייתא says one should not say ברכת המזון silently, but if he did, he fulfilled his obligation. If רבי יהודה allows even לכתחילה and רבי יוסי allows not even בדיעבד, this middle ruling has no author.
steps.simpleTranslation: But what about the ברייתא that teaches: 'A person should not say ברכת המזון in his heart, but if he did, he has fulfilled his obligation.' Whose view is that? Neither רבי יהודה nor רבי יוסי! If רבי יהודה, he allows it even from the outset. If רבי יוסי, he does not allow it even after the fact.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא shows that the fix from Step 20 causes a mirror-image problem with a different ברייתא.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The ברכת המזון ברייתא takes the middle position: not לכתחילה, but valid בדיעבד. That middle position belonged to רבי יהודה under the original reading. Moving רבי יהודה to 'even לכתחילה' leaves this ברייתא without an author, so whichever way we read רבי יהודה, one ברייתא is left unexplained.

keyTerms.meaning: Grace after meals
In his heart, meaning silently, without hearing his own words
He fulfilled his obligation

steps.whatToRemember: There are two ברייתות and only one slot for רבי יהודה. The תרומה ברייתא allows even לכתחילה. The ברכת המזון ברייתא allows only בדיעבד. Whichever way we read רבי יהודה, one ברייתא is left with no author, and the גמרא still needs a resolution.
steps.whyThisMatters: It shows the גמרא checking that every recorded ruling has an author. The tension here sets up the resolution that follows.

phrases.english: But that which was taught in a baraita:

phrases.aramaic: לֹא יְבָרֵךְ אָדָם בִּרְכַּת הַמָּזוֹן בְּלִבּוֹ,
phrases.english: A person should not recite Grace after Meals in his heart,
but if he did recite it so, he fulfilled his obligation. Whose view is this?

phrases.aramaic: לָא רַבִּי יְהוּדָה וְלָא רַבִּי יוֹסֵי!
phrases.english: Neither Rabbi Yehuda nor Rabbi Yosei!
If Rabbi Yehuda, it is allowed even from the outset;

phrases.aramaic: אִי רַבִּי יוֹסֵי — אֲפִילּוּ דִּיעֲבַד נָמֵי לָא!
phrases.english: if Rabbi Yosei, even after the fact it does not count!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Rejects the Step 20 fix by showing it leaves the ברכת המזון ברייתא without an author.
steps.kashyaTarget: The proposal that רבי יהודה allows speech without hearing even לכתחילה.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The ברכת המזון ברייתא holds 'not לכתחילה, valid בדיעבד.' If רבי יהודה allows even לכתחילה and רבי יוסי allows not even בדיעבד, nobody holds the middle view that this ברייתא states.
